被災地が１日も早く復興することを願います。
日本ならどこでも起きる可能性のある規模の地震。
出来ることは国、自治体、個人の全てで防災対策を徹底し被害を減らすこと。

東京で起きた場合の被害をchat GPTに予測してもらいました。

昨日の熊本地震（M7.1・最大震度7）と同規模の地震が東京23区直下で発生した場合、東京の人口・建物・インフラの集中を考えると、熊本よりはるかに大きな被害になる可能性があります。

想定される被害（概算）

👉 死者：約3,000～6,000人
👉 負傷者：約5万～9万人
👉 建物の全壊・焼失：約10万～19万棟
👉 避難者：約200万～300万人
👉 帰宅困難者：約400万人

被害が大きくなる理由

人口・建物が極めて密集している
木造住宅密集地で大規模火災が発生しやすい
鉄道・道路・通信など都市機能への影響が全国に波及する

補足

これは東京都や政府の首都直下地震（M7.3）想定を基に、M7.1相当へ概算したものです。

items.title: “مايكروسوفت” تطلق نموذج ذكاء اصطناعي للأمن السيبراني
items.summary:
“مايكروسوفت” تطلق نموذج ذكاء اصطناعي للأمن السيبراني

أعلنت “مايكروسوفت” إطلاق أول نموذج ذكاء اصطناعي متخصص في الأمن السيبراني، إلى جانب منصة جديدة تعتمد على وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي لأتمتة عمليات الدفاع الإلكتروني، في خطوة تستهدف منافسة كبار مطوري الذكاء الاصطناعي، وعلى رأسهم “OpenAI” و”غوغل” و”أنثروبيك”.

وخلال فعالية أقيمت في مدينة سان فرانسيسكو، كشفت الشركة عن نموذج MAI-Cyber-1-Flash، الذي صُمم خصيصاً لاكتشاف الثغرات الأمنية المعقدة داخل قواعد البرمجيات، ويعمل بالتكامل مع نظام MDASH المخصص لتحليل الثغرات واكتشافها والمساعدة في إصلاحها، بحسب تقرير نشره موقع “تك كرانش”.

منصة جديدة تعتمد على فرق ذكاء اصطناعي
كما كشفت “مايكروسوفت” عن منصة جديدة تحمل اسم Perception، وهي منصة تعتمد على فرق من وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي لتنفيذ مختلف مهام الأمن السيبراني، بدءاً من اكتشاف الثغرات وتحليلها، وصولاً إلى اقتراح حلول وإصلاحها بشكل شبه آلي، مع إمكانية التكامل الكامل مع نظام MDASH.

وأكدت الشركة أن نموذج MAI-Cyber-1-Flash يتفوق من حيث الكفاءة والتكلفة على نماذج المنافسين، استناداً إلى نتائج اختبار Cyber Gym، الذي يعد أحد أبرز المعايير المستخدمة لقياس أداء نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي في الأمن السيبراني.

وقال مصطفى سليمان، الرئيس التنفيذي لوحدة Microsoft AI والمؤسس المشارك لشركة ديب مايند: “يسعدنا الإعلان عن هذه النتائج. لقد دمجنا MAI-Cyber-1-Flash مع GPT 5.4 داخل بيئة MDASH، وحقق أداءً أفضل من جيميناي وGPT 5.5 Cyber وGPT 5.6 Sol وMythos 5 على معيار Cyber Gym، وهو المعيار الذهبي الذي يعتمد عليه القطاع.”

وأضاف أن الشركة بدأت بالفعل في نشر التقنية داخل بيئات الإنتاج.

مواجهة هجمات الذكاء الاصطناعي بالذكاء الاصطناعي
وأوضحت هاييت غالوت، نائبة رئيس “مايكروسوفت” لشؤون الأمن، أن المهاجمين يعتمدون بصورة متزايدة على الذكاء الاصطناعي في تنفيذ الهجمات الإلكترونية، ولذلك صُممت منصة Perception لتمكين المؤسسات من “مواجهة الذكاء الاصطناعي باستخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي، وبالسرعة والحجم نفسيهما اللذين يستخدمهما المهاجمون.”

وتضم المنصة ثلاثة أنواع من فرق الوكلاء الذكية:

– الفرق الحمراء (Red Teams): تحاكي الهجمات المحتملة، وتحدد أساليب المهاجمين والثغرات التي قد يستغلونها.

– الفرق الزرقاء (Blue Teams): تتولى اكتشاف الثغرات الموجودة وتصنيفها وتحديد أولويات معالجتها.

– الفرق الخضراء (Green Teams): تنفذ الإجراءات التصحيحية وتقترح إصلاحات مباشرة للثغرات المكتشفة.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Blasts Centralization of A.I. Power
items.summary: Technologists like Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, have said some of today’s leading A.I. models are too dangerous to be shared and developed without tight controls. But Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and Meta have disagreed, contending that many A.I. models must be developed largely in the open for people to advance the technology and build new businesses. [...] Mark Zuckerberg came out swinging against Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the world’s most valuable artificial intelligence start-ups, saying the way they developed A.I. software could lead to a centralization of power that would narrow people’s access to the transformational technology. [...] In an interview on Tuesday with The New York Times, the 42-year-old chief executive of Meta did not call out Anthropic and OpenAI by name. But he said that if leading research labs wanted to develop A.I. technology in a tightly controlled manner — as Anthropic and OpenAI have done — it would be akin to “abandoning our values” in American tech development and stifle innovation.

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:

"by March of 2028, we will have a full end to end, very talented researcher figuring out completely new architectures."

Not an assistant. Not autocomplete for scientists. A system that does the research that produces the next system.

In 1965 the statistician I. J. Good wrote that the first ultraintelligent machine is the last invention man need ever make. For sixty years that sentence lived in philosophy papers. Altman just put it on a roadmap with a quarter attached.

He also says: "with an affordable amount of spend on tokens, you can do what a 100-person, incredibly great engineering team would do as a startup."

Sixty years of arguing about whether the last invention is possible. Nobody expected the answer to arrive as a delivery date.

items.title: Sam Altman just said something that should worry you more than excite you:
items.summary:
Sam Altman just said something that should worry you more than excite you: 

"AI is close to creating a genie that can grant any wish."

This is EXACTLY why open-source AI matters - and this was Elon's original thesis when he was at OpenAI. 

Right now, the future of all AI power sits with a handful of companies. 

Think: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta. 

They decide who gets access, at what price, under what rules, and on what timeline.

Open-weight models are the only solution to ensuring this "genius in a bottle" power is in check. 

Ultimately, this is also why it matters that NVIDIA, Microsoft, Hugging Face, and dozens of others just signed a joint letter arguing that we need to pivot towards open-weight AI. 

The most powerful technology in human history should not be something a handful of executives dole out to the world on their own terms.

The bull case for open-source AI is simple: don't let five companies hold all the leverage over everyone else.

MIT put the entire course online. it has been free for over twenty years. almost nobody finishes it.

His point: the market never pays in certainties. it pays in probabilities, and a human gut can barely hold one straight. the math that holds ten thousand at once, weighs them, and collapses them into a single call is linear algebra. it is the branch Citadel and OpenAI both pay $400K to hire for.

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: Accenture wins $821M Pentagon AI data platform contract
items.summary:
Discover how federal agencies are applying AI to strengthen cybersecurity, improve operational efficiency and deliver measurable mission outcomes while balancing innovation, governance and human expertise.

The department said its initial order under the contract is focused on “high-impact, measurable mission outcomes that maximize the benefits of commercial pricing.” An Accenture spokesperson did not respond Tuesday to emailed questions about what that work entails. [...] The platform aims to combine more than 1,500 data sources, both commercial and military, to securely provide intelligence, targeting data and more to frontline troops and their commands, the AI office said, calling it “one of [DoD]’s most vital data platforms for AI exploitation and mission advantage.” [...] “The evolution of Advana’s data platform and application ecosystem over the last six years has led to a complex technical and programmatic architecture that we now must rationalize in order to capitalize on the full potential of AI and support warfighting, intelligence, and enterprise needs with the speed, security, and auditability required,” Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg said in a January memo.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Blasts Centralization of A.I. Power
items.summary: Technologists like Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, have said some of today’s leading A.I. models are too dangerous to be shared and developed without tight controls. But Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and Meta have disagreed, contending that many A.I. models must be developed largely in the open for people to advance the technology and build new businesses. [...] Mark Zuckerberg came out swinging against Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the world’s most valuable artificial intelligence start-ups, saying the way they developed A.I. software could lead to a centralization of power that would narrow people’s access to the transformational technology. [...] In an interview on Tuesday with The New York Times, the 42-year-old chief executive of Meta did not call out Anthropic and OpenAI by name. But he said that if leading research labs wanted to develop A.I. technology in a tightly controlled manner — as Anthropic and OpenAI have done — it would be akin to “abandoning our values” in American tech development and stifle innovation.
